report.source_text: The biopsy revealed a basaloid cutaneous lesion consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma, as observed in the H&E histological section (figure 1). Immunohistochemistry was performed, revealing that the lesion exhibited patchy infiltrates positively staining for epithelial membrane antigen, specifically staining the apical aspect of the pseudo glandular cyst (figure 2A). Additionally, there was diffuse positive staining for pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3) (figure 2B).

report.source_text: Under local anaesthesia, the two lesions were completely excised surgically. Subsequent reconstruction of the operative site involved the use of a local flap using adjacent skin to reconstruct and fill the defect created by the surgical excision on the scalp. A rotational flap was used, repositioning surrounding scalp tissue in an arc to effectively cover the excision site.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 20s presented with a 4-month history of a persistent swelling and pruritic lesions on the right posterior scalp. Initial clinical exam found two distinct scalp lesions. Biopsy of the lesions revealed a basaloid cutaneous lesion consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma with supportive immunohistochemical staining. Imaging including sonographic evaluation showed two hypoechoic lesions resembling epidermoid cysts and PET-CT excluded metastatic disease with no abnormal FDG uptake. Surgical excision of the lesions with local flap reconstruction was performed. Although direct histopathological examination of the excised tissue was not fully documented, the diagnosis of PCACC was supported by the initial biopsy, imaging, absence of metastasis, and documented surgical management, consistent with the final diagnosis.
